scope: Uniswap SwapRouter02 V3 single-hop, packed V3 multi-hop, and V2 multi-hop semantic evidence for PQ1 constrained restoration

policy.mechanism: PQ1 restores two V3 single-hop routes, the two packed V3 multi-hop routes, and exactly two V2 multi-hop routes under device-enforced semantics. Every admitted route renders the exact signed zero @.value, recipient address(1) resolves to the signed UserOperation sender, and address(2) refuses. Exact-input amountIn=0 refuses; V3 single-hop nonzero sqrtPriceLimitX96 refuses; V2 renders every signed path address and rejects paths above its renderer cap. Packed V3 renders every full token address and uint24 pool fee, accepts only canonical 20+n*(3+20) byte paths with one through five pools, and derives forward versus reverse presentation from the signed selector so exactOutput is shown in execution/user direction. Labels stay neutral because pre-existing router native currency can fund a WETH9 input even though this transaction cannot fund the router; the rejected amountIn=0 branch is the route to router-held ERC-20 payment. Every other unsupported runtime combination remains an exact known-call hard refusal.

constrained_routes.descriptor_format_key: exactInputSingle((address tokenIn, address tokenOut, uint24 fee, address recipient, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutMinimum, uint160 sqrtPriceLimitX96) params)
exactOutputSingle((address tokenIn, address tokenOut, uint24 fee, address recipient, uint256 amountOut, uint256 amountInMaximum, uint160 sqrtPriceLimitX96) params)
exactInput((bytes path, address recipient, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutMinimum) params)
exactOutput((bytes path, address recipient, uint256 amountOut, uint256 amountInMaximum) params)
swapExactTokensForTokens(uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutMin, address[] path, address to)
swapTokensForExactTokens(uint256 amountOut, uint256 amountInMax, address[] path, address to)

runtime.proxy_claim: The fixed-block contract is not an ERC-1967 implementation/beacon proxy or an EIP-1167 minimal proxy; this is not a claim about every proxy convention.

payment_dependency.payment_semantics: pay(token,payer,recipient,value) wraps native currency only when token==WETH9 and the router native balance covers value; otherwise it transfers tokens already held by the router when payer==address(this), or pulls token funds from payer with transferFrom.

semantic_hazards: recipient address(1) resolves to msg.sender and address(2) resolves to the router itself.
exactInputSingle, packed exactInput, and swapExactTokensForTokens amountIn=0 consume the router's entire tokenIn balance and change the payer to the router.
A nonzero exact-input price limit can make amountIn a cap rather than an exact consumed amount.
A nonzero exact-output price limit permits amountOutReceived to be smaller than the requested amountOut.
Every V2 path address determines a hop, pair, intermediate receiver, and final output token; endpoint-only rendering would hide signed execution effects.
Every packed V3 path byte determines a token address or uint24 fee; its canonical framing is one initial 20-byte token followed by one or more 23-byte fee-and-token hops.

Packed exactInput consumes the path from its first pool forward, while packed exactOutput encodes tokenOut-to-tokenIn and executes recursively in reverse; exactOutput display must therefore reverse both token and fee traversal into input-to-output order.
swapExactTokensForTokens enforces amountOutMin against the final recipient balance delta, while swapTokensForExactTokens computes every hop's required input and enforces amountInMax.
The outer payable value is independent of route amounts; all six constrained formats render the exact signed @.value explicitly and require it to be zero.

PeripheryPayments can wrap pre-existing router native currency when tokenIn is WETH9; router-held ERC-20 payment requires the amountIn=0 router-payer branch, which the admitted exact-input routes reject.

Requiring @.value=0 prevents this transaction from funding the router, but a pre-existing router native balance can still fund a WETH9 input; labels therefore do not claim that the signer necessarily pays the displayed input.
residuals: This is a fixed-block historical receipt for Ethereum chain 1 and does not provide live deployment monitoring.
Blockscout marks the source partially verified rather than fully verified; the 21 repo-owned verified sources were byte-identical to the pinned official release.

The constrained restoration depends on device-verifiable sentinel, amount-zero, price-limit, canonical packed-path framing, complete-path, selector-derived direction, recipient, and outer-value-zero checks; unsupported combinations remain hard refusals.

The v3-periphery v1.3.0 tag is annotated but unsigned; the exact dependency is independently pinned by the swap-router package, lockfile tarball digest, commit/tree, archived source hash, and tarball/source byte equality.
The V2 path renderer is deliberately capped at eight addresses; longer paths remain hard refusals even though the contract can execute them.
The packed V3 path renderer is deliberately capped at five pools; longer paths remain hard refusals even though the contract can execute them.
The known-call Bloom is probabilistic, but all six admitted tuples are asserted against the exact builder set offline.
This evidence grants no production-shipment, fallback, generic signing, legacy-transaction, or blind-signing authority.
